title: From a uniform Holder bound to a valid limiting equation
audience: The reader uses multivariable derivatives, compactness of bounded real sequences, line-segment integration and smooth partitions of unity. Uniform convergence and Holder seminorms are refreshed. Diagonal extraction, derivative compatibility, exponent interpolation and admissibility passage are built in the article. The real L2 test definition and the finite orthonormal-expansion argument are supplied where used in the boundary example.
reader_goals: Reproduce the fixed-chart compactness proof from uniform derivative moduli through C2beta convergence.
Verify which additional margin, continuity and normalization assumptions justify a limiting equation.
Distinguish finite chart localization from local exhaustion and calculate the failure models.
Define weak real-L2 convergence and reproduce the finite orthonormal-expansion proof of the sine/squared-sine boundary example.
prerequisites: Multivariable differential calculus and fundamental theorem of calculus.
Finite smooth atlas and subordinate partitions of unity on a compact manifold.
Basic finite-dimensional matrix norms and scalar compactness.

required_steps: Localize in fixed charts and obtain uniform moduli for every derivative through order two.
Extract on a countable dense set and use finite nets to obtain uniform convergence.
Pass the line-segment integral identity and glue compatible C2 derivatives.
Preserve the alpha bound and prove beta convergence by the interpolation inequality.
Pass the uniform matrix margin before applying joint continuity of F.
Check normalization and a concrete nonlinear C0 passage, and distinguish local exhaustion.
Define weak L2 convergence, derive coefficient decay from orthonormality and the finite projection identity, and test squared sines against constant one.
